text:
Alex Carter: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — I want to propose we move forward with a "service tessellation" approach to break inference-core into smaller, ownership-aligned pieces. Link to RFC: https://rwd.internal/rfcs/2026/service-tessellation :eyes:

Tess Nguyen: +1 on principle. can you summarize the minimal set of interfaces we'd need for the first phase?

Alex Carter: Minimal: (1) request-router (stateless routing & auth), (2) model-manager (model lifecycle, variants), (3) kv-cache-proxy (prefix + KV cache), (4) exec-adapter (runtime execution surface). We keep the old monolith as a facade for 3 months.

Morgan Li: Tradeoffs: more RPCs -> latency risk. but we gain clear ownership and safer migrations. we should measure p95 impact with synthetic traces.

Daniela Ortiz: Concern: transactions / session affinity for multi-turn chat. If we split, how do we keep KV cache locality?

Alex Carter: plan: keep session affinity via sticky routing at request-router for now. kv-cache-proxy will present a consistent local API: `GET /cache/{session}/{prefix}`. We'll colocate kv-cache-proxy with exec-adapter in early rollout to avoid cross-hop hot paths.

Samir Patel: +1. Also propose a compatibility shim so existing clients can call the facade while we incrementally flip routes. simple proxy that rewrites headers and forwards to the new services.

Tess Nguyen: For rollout, I'd propose phases: 
- Phase 0: read-only model-manager extracted (no write APIs) behind feature flag.
- Phase 1: read-write model-manager, kv-cache-proxy in colocated mode.
- Phase 2: request-router split + canary 5% traffic.
- Phase 3: traffic ramp + retire facade.

Morgan Li: We need contract tests. I can add a tiny harness that runs proto/gRPC contract checks and p95 latency gates. Also add chaos tests for cross-service failures.

Daniela Ortiz: On state migrations: if we ever move to sharded kv, we must version the cache keys. Add a version header `X-Cache-Schema: v1` so we can do live migrations without invalidation storms.

Alex Carter: good call. add `X-Request-Trace` header too. And we'll expose metrics: `service.*.rpc.duration`, `service.*.errors`, `kv.cache.hit_rate`, `router.affinity_miss`. Those metrics are required for signoff.

Samir Patel: ops notes: infra needs a drain/redirect playbook, and a plan to avoid sticky IPs holding onto old listeners. I'll raise infra ticket and assign a runbook: INFRA-4768.

Tess Nguyen: testing checklist draft: contract tests, 10k synthetic tokens at realistic concurrency, rollout abort criteria: >5% p95 regression or >1% errors for 10m.

Alex Carter: sample proto for router->exec (very small):
```proto
syntax = "proto3";
package rwd.exec;
message ExecRequest { string session_id = 1; string model = 2; bytes prompt = 3; map<string,string> meta = 4; }
message ExecResponse { bytes tokens = 1; int32 status = 2; }
service Exec { rpc Run(ExecRequest) returns (ExecResponse); }
```

Morgan Li: nit: use `bytes prompt` only for now, we'll add streaming later. For batching, exec-adapter should support a `BatchRun` unary that accepts repeated requests.

Daniela Ortiz: ownership: who owns `kv-cache-proxy`? we should create a short-lived cross-team pod: eng-runtime + eng-platform pairing for first 2 sprints.

Alex Carter: Suggest owners: Tess (product/owner for phase), Morgan (runtime technical lead), Samir (infra readiness), Daniela (data & migration). I'll open an ADR and assign.

infra-bot: Reminder — cluster quota request required for canary nodes. Opened ticket INFRA-4772 and linked to this thread.

Tess Nguyen: I'll draft the rollout doc and link in RFC comments by EOD tomorrow. Anyone want the write-up assigned?

Samir Patel: I can take the infra section. will add deploy playbook and drain steps.

Morgan Li: I'll author contract tests and perf harness.

Daniela Ortiz: I'll write the migration strategy and key-versioning plan.

Alex Carter: Great. Last thing: timeline target = Q2 sprint 3 for Phase 1 extraction and internal canary by ops. If blockers, we push. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
